definition: The family of decoder-only Transformer language models introduced by OpenAI that generate text left to right.
details: GPT established the recipe that dominates modern LLMs: pre-train an autoregressive Transformer on a large corpus to predict the next token, then adapt it. The original paper showed that generative pre-training plus discriminative fine-tuning beat prior task-specific models; later generations (GPT-2, GPT-3, GPT-4) scaled the same idea into chat assistants and tool-using agents.

explainer.lead: GPT is a family of language models that learn by predicting the next piece of text, then continue that process to write one token at a time. Its combination of large-scale pre-training and later adaptation became a foundation for modern chat assistants and tool-using agents.

tiers.eli5: GPT is like someone playing a giant game of guessing the next word. After practising on a huge collection of writing, it can keep adding one likely piece after another to answer questions or write text.
tiers.practitioner: GPT-style systems use a decoder-only Transformer trained autoregressively on a large corpus, then adapt the pre-trained model for the intended use. Generation proceeds left to right, with each new token conditioned on the existing sequence. GPT-2, GPT-3, and GPT-4 show how this approach was scaled into chat assistants and tool-using agents.
tiers.paperLevel: For tokens x_1 ... x_T, the autoregressive objective factorizes the sequence probability as p(x) = product over t of p(x_t | x_<t), using a decoder-only Transformer. The original GPT work paired generative pre-training on a large corpus with discriminative fine-tuning and outperformed earlier task-specific models. Each prediction is conditioned on preceding tokens rather than future tokens.

explainer.example: Given the prefix “The cat sat on the”, the model predicts a next token such as “mat”. It then adds that token to the sequence and uses the longer prefix to predict what comes next.

usedIn.name: Chat assistants
usedIn.detail: Later GPT generations scaled next-token pre-training into conversational systems.

usedIn.name: Tool-using agents
usedIn.detail: Later GPT generations extended the same approach to agents that use tools.

usedIn.name: Discriminative language tasks
usedIn.detail: The original work fine-tuned the generatively pre-trained model for specific tasks.

components.name: Large corpus: supplies text for generative pre-training.
Decoder-only Transformer: models each token from the tokens before it.
Next-token objective: provides the autoregressive training signal.
Adaptation stage: adjusts the pre-trained model for later tasks or uses.

flow: Pre-train the Transformer on a large text corpus.
At each position, predict the next token from the preceding tokens.
Adapt the pre-trained model; the original work used discriminative fine-tuning.
Generate text by repeatedly appending a predicted token and predicting again.
explainer.origin: OpenAI introduced GPT as a decoder-only Transformer language model. The original paper showed that generative pre-training followed by discriminative fine-tuning could beat earlier task-specific models.
explainer.whyItMatters: GPT established a reusable recipe: learn broadly through next-token prediction, then adapt the resulting model. Scaling that recipe across later generations helped shape modern large language models and their uses.
